propositions: Two reducer cache writers use the same fixed `.cache.json.tmp` artifact, allowing overlapping file descriptors to mutate the visible final file after one writer renames it into place.
Concurrent reductions of different event generations can splice fields from independent valid envelopes, producing a cache with the current generation hash but stale state that bypasses replay.
The corrupt-CREATE cache publication in `process_create` must be routed through `write_cache` to ensure all cache writers share the same atomic replace and cleanup policy.
Cache publication must use the canonical `fsutil.atomic_write` mechanism with unique temporary files and proper cleanup to prevent FileNotFoundError and coherency violations.
Concurrent reducer cache writes must guarantee that a current-hash cache hit exactly equals the result of cache-bypassing deterministic replay.
